Recall probability by study position

  • Show All Code
  • Hide All Code
On this page

On this page

  • Configure this run
  • Load data and select trials
  • Plot recall by study position

A serial position curve (SPC) shows how often participants recall an item as a function of its position on the study list. A recall at any output position counts.

Parameter Meaning
data_paths, data_labels Response files in HDF5 format and their labels, in matching order. List each file once.
trial_queries, labels One trial query and label per condition. The queries apply to every file. Use [None] and ["All lists"] to include all eligible trials in one condition.
comparison "datasets" gives one figure per condition, with one curve per file. "conditions" overlays the conditions from a single file on one figure.
complete_lists_only Set to True to exclude trials with any padded study positions.
max_subjects Maximum number of participants per file, starting with the lowest IDs. Zero includes everyone.
confidence_level, plot_seed Confidence level for the interval around each mean, expressed as a fraction, and the random seed for resampling participants.
project_root Base directory for relative input and output paths.
output_dir, figure_dir Figures are saved in output_dir unless you supply a separate figure_dir.
figure_str Figure filename stem. Use an empty string to display figures without saving them.
color_cycle, contrast_name Colors in curve order and an optional legend title. The legend appears when a figure has multiple curves.
ylim, yticks Lower and upper limits of the recall-probability axis and optional tick positions.

The notebook displays each figure separately. Saving a single figure writes <figure_str>.png. With several figures, each filename includes the condition number and label, for example spc_1_immediate.png for a first condition labeled “Immediate” and a stem of spc.

Configure this run

Input files, trial queries, and figure settings 
from typing import Literal

type ComparisonMode = Literal["conditions", "datasets"]

data_paths = ["data/Dupertuys2026.h5"]
data_labels = ["Observed"]
trial_queries = ["data['list_type'] == 1", "data['list_type'] == 2", "data['list_type'] == 3"]
labels = ["Mixed", "Pure emotional", "Pure neutral"]
# Use "datasets" for one figure per condition or "conditions" to overlay conditions from one file.
comparison: ComparisonMode = "datasets"
complete_lists_only = True
max_subjects = 0              # Zero includes all participants.
confidence_level = 0.95
plot_seed = 0

project_root = None
output_dir = "results/spc"
figure_dir = None             # Defaults to output_dir.
figure_str = "spc"            # An empty name displays figures without saving.

# Optional plot settings for parameterized runs.
color_cycle = None
contrast_name = None
ylim = (0, 1)
yticks = None

Load data and select trials

Relative paths use the project directory. The data guide describes the expected file format.

Install JAXCMR in Colab 
import sys

if "google.colab" in sys.modules:
    %pip install --upgrade "jaxcmr @ git+https://github.com/githubpsyche/jaxcmr.git@main"
Import plotting and dataset operations 
import re

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

from jaxcmr.analyses.spc import plot_spc
from jaxcmr.dataset import select_conditions
from jaxcmr.examples import copy_example_inputs
from jaxcmr.helpers import load_data, resolve_project_path, resolve_project_root
from jaxcmr.plotting import add_analysis_legend, comparison_panels, save_figure
Load response files 
root = resolve_project_root(project_root)
copy_example_inputs(data_paths, base_dir=root)
datasets = [load_data(resolve_project_path(path, root), max_subjects=max_subjects) for path in data_paths]

With complete_lists_only=True, the selection excludes any trial with a padded study position. This includes shorter lists stored alongside longer ones.

Build a trial mask for each condition 
masks_by_dataset = []
for dataset in datasets:
    selections = select_conditions(dataset, trial_queries, complete_lists_only=complete_lists_only)
    masks_by_dataset.append([selection.mask for selection in selections])

Plot recall by study position

Each point is the mean of the participants’ recall probabilities at that position. Error bars show bootstrap confidence intervals for that mean. If an item appeared more than once on a list, recalling it credits each of its study positions once.

Draw and save each comparison 
panels = comparison_panels(
    datasets, masks_by_dataset, data_labels, labels, mode=comparison
)
for number, panel in enumerate(panels, start=1):
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.4 if len(panel["labels"]) > 1 else 4.8, 3.2))
    plot_spc(panel["datasets"], panel["trial_masks"], axis=ax, labels=panel["labels"],
             color_cycle=color_cycle, confidence_level=confidence_level, bootstrap_seed=plot_seed)

    title = data_labels[0] if comparison == "conditions" else panel["title"]
    ax.set_title(title, loc="left", fontsize=12)
    ax.set_xlabel("Study position", fontsize=12)
    ax.set_ylabel("Recall probability", fontsize=12)
    ax.tick_params(labelsize=10)
    ax.set_ylim(ylim)
    if yticks is not None:
        ax.set_yticks(yticks)
    if len(panel["labels"]) > 1:
        add_analysis_legend(ax, contrast_name)

    if figure_str:
        suffix = None
        if len(panels) > 1:
            label = re.sub(r"\W+", "_", panel["title"].casefold()).strip("_")
            suffix = f"{number}_{label}".rstrip("_")
        save_figure(resolve_project_path(figure_dir or output_dir, root), figure_str,
                    suffix=suffix, figure=fig)
    else:
        fig.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
    plt.close(fig)
